layout_notes: Published corner numbering for Streets varies (12 to 14 turns depending on the layout and who counted the skidpad), so the sources were mapped to the sim profile's zones by sequence, not by their turn numbers. The Bowl is Turn 8 in the written source's numbering and Turn 11 in some published guides.

Every source predates the real track's 2025 repave/refurbishment. The sim mod models the classic layout, so the older references — berms, pavement seams, the Bowl's banking — are the right vintage here. The real track has since changed.

Colin Lucas teaches the student line on purpose — his own words are that it is not the full racing line: braking done early and in a straight line, whole track used. The written source (Karl) is a fast amateur in a front-wheel-drive car whose deep-entry choices are flagged where they are his car's, not the corner's.

source.layout_note: Instructor narrating three CW laps, student line. Merged with Karl's written turn-by-turn (kls2.com, Mazdaspeed 3, Feb 2020) and forum notes; see sources.

tips: Use the pit exit to maximise the radius — no braking needed
Hit the inside berm; a brief lift is the most it asks (Karl)
Half to two-thirds throttle is plenty until it's familiar (Colin)
Turn 4 is a tight right — the most challenging corner here (Karl); drivers get brave off Turn 3 and are startled by how tight it is
Don't accelerate too quickly up the hill — it flattens and falls off to the right, and people lose it there (Colin)
Turn 6 is about setting up Turn 7's entry; speed is picking up
It sits on a slight crest at the end of the back straight and is blind — terrifying near 100 mph until it's learned (Karl)
It can be driven almost in a straight line, and nearly flat, once you know it (Karl)
The honest intermediate step is a slight brake tap before 9B (Karl)

1.character: The downhill left after the Turn 1 kink — effectively a 180 with a decreasing radius, and every source gives it the same lesson: the apex is much later than it looks. Stay mid-track, resist tucking in early, turn in late onto the inside berm, and let the car run only about halfway out before collecting it for Turn 3. Karl's note from the real car: hit the apex early and there is no padding at the exit — the corner earns respect on lap one.
1.name: Turn 2

tips.text: Turn in later than you think — stay mid-track, it's a late-apex corner

tips: Brake in a straight line and get it done — don't trail deep into it
Use the second berm; let it run halfway out, not all the way

tips.text: Once it's turned, get back on the gas down the hill

2.character: Wide double-apex uphill left. Two apexes — the berms either side — and more than one workable line through it. Karl's job list: hit both apexes tightly and wrestle the car to stay left on exit for the tight right that follows; his verdict is that it isn't the corner that makes the lap, but a sloppy exit taxes the next one. The section was the grippy, repaved part of the old track, and the forum notes say don't be shy on the gas.
2.name: Turn 3
tips: Double apex — clip both berms

tips.text: Don't be shy on the gas — it climbs and the grip is there

tips: Exit still on the left — the tight right (Turn 4) is waiting

3.character: The long, basically flat sweeping left that feeds the Bowl — the fastest corner on the track outside the straights. Karl worked up to nearly full throttle here. Exit position matters more than the corner itself: come out mid-track rather than tucked tight (2/3 out is plenty, per Colin), then bring the car fully left to set up the Bowl braking zone.
3.name: Turn 7

tips.text: Build to nearly full throttle — commit, the speed carries to the Bowl

tips: Exit mid-track, not pinned to the inside
Bring it fully left for the Bowl braking

4.character: The short braking and turn-in into the Bowl. It asks for far less brake than instinct says — the 20-degree banking does the slowing — but what braking there is must be finished before turn-in. Karl used the pavement seams as his markers (the apex cone can move): full commitment by the first seam, apex at the second.
4.name: Bowl Entry

tips.text: A light tap is enough — the banking does the work; get it done before turn-in

tips: Aim for the second pavement seam, not the cone — cones move
Commit to the inside early and let the banking catch the car

5.character: The banked carousel — about 20 degrees of banking sweeping roughly half a circle. The banking is grip: tuck into the inside, let the car take the bank, then slowly unwind the wheel as you accelerate and run all the way out to the left. The standard mistake is driving it like a flat corner — braking hard on entry and waiting to get back to power while the banking sits there unused.
5.name: The Bowl

tips.text: It's a tap, not a stop — the banking holds the car
Unwind the wheel and feed power early — the banking is grip, use it

tips: All the way in on entry, all the way out to the left on exit

6.character: The braking complex after the chicane, running into the downhill off-camber left that ends the lap's fast half. Colin's student briefing is blunt: bleed off ALL your speed before the off-camber left — a lot of spins end up there — and do the braking in a straight line, never around the turn itself; clipping in too hard is how people end up backwards. Karl's approach from the other side: sacrifice the preceding right to carry back-straight speed as long as possible, then brake hard, and make this left as broad and fast as the grip allows.
6.name: Turn 11

tips.text: Brake straight and early — never brake around the off-camber left

tips: Bleed off all the speed before the off-camber left — it's the spin corner
Don't clip in too hard — that's how it goes backwards

tips.text: Broad and fast once it's turned — don't strangle the exit

7.character: The final right, a roughly 180-degree turn on the skidpad's good grip, onto the front straight — the longest straight on the track, which makes this exit the lap's paycheck (Colin calls it the most important turn here). The pad lets you choose tight against the cones or a deeper, larger-radius hook; Karl tried both all day and found the limit was front-tire adhesion on exit either way, and that his front-straight speed actually went DOWN as he pushed harder — wheelspin. Feed the power in progressively and keep it hooked up; sliding here looks free and costs seconds.
7.name: Skidpad

tips.text: Feed power progressively — wheelspin out of here taxes the whole front straight
Keep it hooked up — sliding on the pad looks free and costs seconds

tips: Pick the line that gets you to full power earliest — the pad allows either
Use the whole track on exit; you've paid for it (Colin)
